title: The Long Silence
subtitle: Faithful-modern homage — original prose
source: Liu Cixin, Remembrance of Earth's Past (Three-Body trilogy, 2008-2010) — engine/theory in canon/SOURCE_NOTES.md
mandates: #2 No sag — theory dramatised under pressure, velocity protected
Idea-as-detonation: one perfect-calibre set-piece per movement

cast.Ada Reyes: the Analyst (Mvt I) — reads the loudness, writes the unread first-true-line, dies in I
cast.Marcus Hale: the Sender (Mvt I) — argues the Hail out of hope-into-hubris, not revenge
cast.Cole Ridgeway: the Strategist (Mvt II) — deduces the law, forges the Reckoners' deterrent
cast.Nadia Brandt: the Cop/ballast (Mvt II) — native-English tuning fork
cast.Esme Calderon: the Inheritor (Mvt III) — her mercy fails the deterrent

chapters.title: Prologue
chapters.pov: Marcus Hale (the Sender) + a console woman (proto-Analyst seed)
chapters.setting: The Deep Listening Array, the night of the Hail
beats: A celebration for the loudest act in the species' history (PP-002)
Hale's sympathetic, arguable case: silence = loneliness, not danger (PP-002)
The console woman's quiet counter: 'they already know how alone they are — that's why it's quiet'
The Hail goes out — eleven minutes, silent on the lawn, light-fast toward the forest (PP-003)
chapters.turn: Humanity lights the match, celebrating; the dread is seeded in one mouth, unanswered

chapters.title: The Brightening
chapters.setting: Correlation room at the DLA; weeks after the Hail
beats: A calibration run; eighty years of folded sky that won't clean (discovery under pressure, anti-sag)
The noise IS the planet — the broadcast-folly recoded as DATA, a brightening dot (PP-001)
The funny thought then the cold one: we are the only light on in the street
The bubble of loudness; the catalogue of porches inside earshot; light is fast AND slow
The first true line written down, read by no one for nineteen years (PP-010)
chapters.turn: The folly becomes a thing that can be SEEN, and therefore aimed at

chapters.title: The Reply
chapters.pov: Ada Reyes (the Analyst), close-third; Marcus Hale present
chapters.setting: The DLA; months later; first the data, then the closed briefing
beats: The reply arrives — and it is not a message, it is a vector and a duration: a countdown (PP-001)
Ada is the one who realises it isn't a greeting; the room argues, Hale clings to hope
The math of the countdown: long enough that no one in this room survives it (relay seeded)
Hale's hope curdles privately into the first guilt; the species' optimism indicted, gently
Decision: tell the world or hold it — the politics of a planet that cannot un-broadcast
chapters.turn: First contact is revealed as a lit fuse; the countdown starts ticking and never stops

chapters.title: The Quiet Sabotage
chapters.pov: Ada Reyes (the Analyst), close-third; a physicist colleague
chapters.setting: The DLA + a high-energy physics lab feeding it data; a year or two on
beats: The Net's first effects: high-energy physics results stop making sense — subtly, maddeningly
Ada connects the corrupted detectors to the countdown: something is already here, watching, capping us
Grounded dread: the enemy fears our FUTURE; it is keeping us from the leap (technological explosion, dramatised)
A scientist breaks under the impossibility of trustworthy data — the human cost of the cap
Ada ages into the work; hands off to a successor; her warning still unread (PP-010, relay handoff begins)
chapters.turn: The abstract threat becomes a present, patient hand on the species' throat

chapters.title: Meridian Reach
chapters.pov: the relay watch at the DLA (Ada's successor); intercut crew of the Meridian Reach
chapters.setting: The DLA deep-space relay + the crewed vessel Meridian Reach in transit
beats: Establish the Meridian Reach and a few of its ~40 crew quickly, with real warmth (bond before we bury)
Routine transit through a known corridor near the relay; nothing seems wrong
Quiet seeding: weeks earlier, Net microprobes anchored something across the corridor (reader half-knows)
The watch at the DLA notices an anomaly too late to matter; the helplessness of watching a feed
chapters.turn: Everything is in place; the ship is on the line; the chapter ends a breath before the cut

chapters.title: The Cut
chapters.pov: the relay watch at the DLA (external, on the feed) — NOT inside the ship
chapters.setting: The DLA relay room, watching the Meridian Reach cross the Filament
beats: DETONATION: the ship crosses the monomolecular filament at transit speed
For one or two seconds nothing appears wrong — the cut is too clean to see (the delay IS the horror)
The ship begins to come apart along parallel planes; lights still on in each separating slab; people in cross-section
The watchers understand a half-beat after the reader does; trust the image, never caption the awe
Aftermath, flat and small: a debris field of neat sheets; the countdown now physical, personal, proven
chapters.turn: Being found means death delivered by something that does not even hate you; Movement I closes on dread

chapters.title: The Children of the Clock
chapters.setting: A defended Earth, ~two generations after the Hail; a city under the countdown
beats: Establish the world a century-ish on: born into certainty of an arriving end; the strange flourishing and despair of it
Brandt's job: she polices the Reckoners' compound (introduce the institution from the OUTSIDE, despised)
The cap still holds — no breakthrough physics in a hundred years; the human texture of stalled progress
Brandt's dry, profane-warm native idiom is the tuning fork; she thinks the Reckoners are ghouls
Seed Cole Ridgeway as the strange new analyst the Reckoners just pulled in — Brandt's first read of him
chapters.turn: The countdown is now the water everyone swims in; the deterrent's keepers are hated; Ridgeway arrives

chapters.title: The Shape of the Forest
chapters.setting: The Reckoners' compound; the deep-archive of failed strategies
beats: Ridgeway reads a century of failed defence ideas; deduces WHY none can work (the law, clause by clause, UNDER PRESSURE — anti-sag)
The two axioms + chain of suspicion + technological explosion DRAMATISED via his arguments with skeptics, not narrated
His one partial, contested near-statement of the law (PP-009) — the closest the book comes to saying it
Brandt watches him work; the ballast keeps it human; he frightens her more than the ghouls did
He sees the only card: we can't win, can't run, can't hide — but we can make ourselves not worth the risk
chapters.turn: Ridgeway grasps the law whole; the deterrent is conceivable but monstrous

chapters.title: A Hand Offered in the Dark
chapters.setting: Earth + a small, secret, hopeful counter-effort to signal goodwill to a NEARER quiet listener
beats: A faction tries the thing Hale tried in miniature: offer provable goodwill to a different, nearer silent star
Ridgeway argues it cannot work — goodwill is UNVERIFIABLE across the dark (the chain of suspicion, paid)
The gesture goes out anyway; the answer (or the silence) proves the law: distance = death (PP-005)
Human cost: the people who needed to believe in kindness; Brandt buries one of them
Ridgeway is now certain; the despised deterrent is the only morality the forest permits
chapters.turn: The last hope of a friendly universe dies; the deterrent stops being monstrous and becomes necessary

chapters.title: The Reckoners
chapters.setting: The forging of the dead-man deterrent; the politics of building a suicide system
beats: Ridgeway forges the mutual-exposure deterrent: a dead-man system that broadcasts the ENEMY's address if Earth is struck (PP-006)
The cruelty: it only works if the keeper of the pin will actually doom everyone, including humanity
Brandt is recruited to GUARD the pin she despised; her arc turns — the ghouls were holding the line
The world hates the Reckoners precisely because they are the price of survival
Seed the next runner: Esme Calderón, young, here, the one who will one day hold the pin
chapters.turn: Humanity's one card is laid: be a suicide bomber holding everyone's coordinates; an uneasy peace begins

chapters.title: One Pass
chapters.pov: Sgt. Nadia Brandt (external witness) + the doomed fleet's edge
chapters.setting: Near-Earth space; the species' assembled defensive fleet meets the single-object weapon
beats: Before the deterrent fully arms, the enemy tests us: a single object enters the system at relativistic speed
Humanity's entire defensive fleet — a century of hope and steel — moves to meet it, confident
DETONATION: the single object makes ONE PASS and ends the fleet; unanswerable, indifferent, calibre-perfect (PP-007)
Echo the Filament: cleanness, scale, no malice; the Meridian Reach was the rehearsal, this is the recital
Brandt watches it the way Park watched the cut; the deterrent is now the ONLY thing left
chapters.turn: Brute defence is proven impossible forever; the deterrent is the species' last and only wall

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.setting: The decades after the fleet; an uneasy stalemate held on the pin; Brandt hands off
beats: The deterrent holds; a strange grim peace; the species learns, at last, to be QUIET (the title, dramatised)
Brandt ages out, like Ada did; trains Esme; the relay's human pulse passes again
What the long quiet costs the species' soul: living as a held breath, a finger on a doom
Brandt's last word — the ballast's plain truth about what they bought and what it cost
Baton to Esme + Movement III; the clock, much smaller now, ticks toward a zero someone alive will see
chapters.turn: Peace bought with a permanent threat to everyone; Brandt dies; Esme inherits the pin

movements_remaining.remaining_beats: III.1 Esme Calderon inherits the Reckoners' pin; III.2 her mercy fails the deterrent (PP-006); III.3 the Quietus — relativistic dust scours the inner system — DETONATION (PP-009, PP-010); III.4 deep-time coda, one small human act (PP-008); III.5 original dedication
